1.d4 f5 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3.strategy: A natural developing move: the knight takes control of e4 and d5, and White stays free to fianchetto the bishop or to build a broad centre. Black has not yet developed the knight, so White can also play for space in the centre.

1.d4 f5 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Nh6.strategy: An offbeat move that parks the knight on the edge to keep f6 clear, so that the bishop on g7 and later the rook on f8 press at once, and keeps the option of rerouting it to f7 or f5. It is less active than the natural development, and White can take a broad centre at once.
1.d4 f5 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Nh6.name: Dutch Defence: Bladel Variation
1.d4 f5 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Nh6.background: Max Euwe introduced it against Salo Flohr in a small tournament at Bladel in the Netherlands in 1969, held in memory of Richard Reti, and the game was drawn. The line has been played hardly at all since and has little established theory.
